arms.description: Participants randomized to this arm will consume 2% fat cow's milk twice daily for 12 weeks.
arms.label: 2% Fat Cows Milk

arms.description: Participants randomized to this arm will consume standard soy milk twice daily for 12 weeks.
arms.label: Standard Soy Milk

eligibility.criteria_text:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Children with overweight/obesity
* Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and an MRI PDFF \>10%
* Known NAFLD or elevated ALT for sex (\>22 for females and \>26 for males)

Exclusion Criteria:

* MRI-PDFF \<10%
* Baseline habitual (\>3 days per week) consumption of soy foods
* Allergy to soy or cow's milk protein
* Inability to undergo MRI
* Recent (past 8 weeks) antibiotic exposure
* Treatment for existing endocrine disorders

interventions.description: Consumption of commercially available soy milk
interventions.name: Standard Soy Milk

interventions.description: Consumption of commercially available 2% cow's milk
interventions.name: 2% Fat Cow's Milk

outcomes.description: Change in liver disease severity, measured using magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF). A relative PDFF change of 30% correlates with histologic improvement in patients with NAFLD and is commonly used in clinical trials.

outcomes.measure: Change in serum aminotransferase levels (ALT, aspartate aminotransferase [AST], GGT, alkaline phosphatase [ALP])
Change in high- and low-density lipoprotein (HDL-C, LCL-C) levels
Change in testosterone, estrogen and sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG) levels
Change in thyroid function (TSH and Free T4)
Change in serum metabolome and lipidome
Change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure

trial.brief_summary: A randomized, controlled study of standard soy milk consumption compared to 2% fat cow's milk consumption in children with Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD). The investigators hypothesize that the daily consumption of soy isoflavones found in the soy milk will be beneficial in reducing NAFLD and other obesity-related comorbidities. The investigators do not expect any adverse endocrine or metabolomic effects from the consumption of soy isoflavones.
trial.brief_title: Impact of Soymilk on Liver Disease Severity of Children With Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD)
